name: Slovenia
tagline: Alps, karst caves, vineyards and 46 kilometres of coast, all within two hours of each other.
summary: Slovenia is the size of Wales and contains a proper alpine range, one of the world's great cave systems, Mediterranean coast, and more forest cover than almost any country in Europe. It has been quietly excellent at sustainable tourism for a decade and the capital pedestrianised its centre in 2007 without much fuss. Everything is close, which is the whole point.

season.note: June and September are ideal: the high trails are open, the lakes are swimmable and Bled is not solid. Winter gives cheap alpine skiing and thermal spas in the east.

getting_around: Distances are tiny — Ljubljana to the coast is 90 minutes, to the Alps one hour. Buses beat trains for the mountains. A car helps in the Soča valley and the Karst.
food: Potica: a rolled nut cake, at every celebration
Štruklji, dumplings rolled with anything from tarragon to cottage cheese
Wine from three distinct regions, almost none of it exported

festivals.name: Wine harvest and St Martin's Day

know: A vignette is required for motorways and checked automatically.
Cave temperatures sit around 8°C year-round; bring a layer even in August.
The Julian Alps are limestone — via ferrata is common and needs real equipment.

regions.name: The Julian Alps
regions.summary: Triglav, two famous lakes, and the turquoise Soča river running to Italy.

cities.name: Bled
cities.summary: An island church in a glacial lake under a cliff-top castle — the most photographed thing in the country and still lovely at 7 am.
highlights: Rowing to the island in a pletna, and ringing the wishing bell
The 6 km lakeside path, flat and swimmable at intervals
Vintgar gorge, on boardwalks over the water

experiences.name: The pletna, rowed standing
experiences.summary: A boat design and a rowing licence handed down through the same families since 1740; there is no engine on the lake by law.

cities.name: Bovec & the Soča
cities.summary: An alpine valley on an unreally turquoise river, and the front line of the Isonzo battles above it.
highlights: Rafting and kayaking on the Soča in early summer
The Walk of Peace: open-air museums along the 1915–17 front
The Vršič pass, 50 hairpins built by Russian prisoners of war

experiences.name: The Walk of Peace
experiences.summary: Trenches, chapels and cemeteries left in place along the mountain front where 300,000 died; the signage is unusually honest.

regions.name: Ljubljana, the Karst & the Coast
regions.summary: A small green capital, the caves that gave 'karst' its name, and a Venetian coastal town.

cities.name: Ljubljana
cities.summary: A capital of 300,000 with a car-free centre, a castle on the hill and Plečnik's architecture holding it together.
highlights: Plečnik's bridges, market colonnade and library — one architect's whole city
The riverside bars on summer evenings
Metelkova, a squatted former barracks turned art complex

cities.name: Postojna & Škocjan
cities.summary: Twenty-four kilometres of cave entered by underground train, and a canyon inside a mountain nearby.
highlights: Olms — blind cave salamanders that live a century
Škocjan's underground gorge, 146 metres deep, on a footbridge

experiences.name: The bridge over the Škocjan gorge
experiences.summary: A river 100 metres below you, inside a mountain, crossed on a suspended footbridge. Quieter and more astonishing than its famous neighbour.

cities.name: Piran
cities.summary: A Venetian town on a spit, with a salt pan beside it worked the same way since the 14th century.
highlights: Tartini square, and the campanile modelled on San Marco
Sečovlje salt pans, harvested by hand
Swimming off the rocks below the walls
